title: 5 Common Bookkeeping Mistakes in Nepal and How to Prevent Them
metaDescription: Avoid costly tax penalties and audit delays. Discover the 5 most frequent bookkeeping errors made by Nepalese businesses and how to fix them.
h1: Common Bookkeeping Mistakes and How to Prevent Them
directAnswer: The most common bookkeeping mistakes in Nepal include failing to reconcile bank statements monthly, issuing sales invoices without recording the buyer's PAN, mixing personal expenses with company accounts, claiming VAT input tax on non-qualifying purchases, and delaying monthly TDS deposits past the 25th of the Nepali month. Establishing automated workflows eliminates these risks.
author: Lalitpur Advisory Research Desk

sections.h2: The 5 Most Damaging Bookkeeping Errors in Nepal
sections.contentHtml:
During our diagnostic evaluations of SME records across Lalitpur and Kathmandu, five recurring errors routinely trigger IRD tax disputes and audit qualifications:

1. Unreconciled Bank Balances

Failing to match accounting ledgers against bank statements leaves unrecorded bank charges, bounced cheques, and duplicate entries unnoticed for months.

2. Claiming VAT Credit on Ineligible Items

Under VAT Act 2052 rules, input VAT on staff entertainment, passenger vehicles (above threshold), and personal consumption cannot be offset against sales VAT.

3. Missing Buyer PAN on Invoices Over NPR 10,000

Under IRD billing directives, invoices exceeding prescribed limits must capture the purchaser's verified PAN; failure invites billing penalties.

4. Delays in Withholding Tax (e-TDS) Verification

Failing to verify TDS entries on the IRD portal creates mismatches, preventing suppliers from claiming tax credit during their annual audit.

5. Disregarding Petty Cash Vouchers

Accumulating thousands of rupees in undocumented small cash expenses without physical signed vouchers results in disallowance by auditors.

faqs.question: What happens if our company makes an error in a filed VAT return?
faqs.answer: An amended return (Sanshodhit D-01) can be filed with the Inland Revenue Department, though it may incur interest charges if additional tax is payable.
